description: A fuller benchmark covering SQL edge cases across NULL semantics, joins, window functions, date boundaries, and aggregation logic.

tasks.question: List customer ids whose cancelled_at is NULL and paid_at is not NULL.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (customer_id INTEGER, paid_at TEXT, cancelled_at TEXT);
inserts: INSERT INTO orders VALUES (4, NULL, NULL);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE cancelled_at IS NULL AND paid_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY customer_id;
hidden_variants: SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE cancelled_at IS NULL AND paid_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY customer_id;

tasks.question: Return customer ids that have placed at least one order.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INTEGER); CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER);
inserts: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (2); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (3);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (10, 1); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 2);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (12, 3); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (13, 3);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id ORDER BY c.customer_id;
hidden_variants: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (1,2,3) ORDER BY customer_id;

tasks.question: For each customer with more than one paid order, return the total amount paid.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE payments (customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL, status TEXT);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM payments WHERE status = 'paid' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY customer_id;
hidden_variants: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM payments WHERE status = 'paid' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY customer_id;

tasks.question: Return order ids for June 2025, inclusive of June 30 but not July 1.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INTEGER, order_date TEXT);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-06-01' AND order_date < '2025-07-01' ORDER BY order_id;
hidden_variants: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-06-01' AND order_date < '2025-07-01' ORDER BY order_id;

tasks.question: Return customers and their order counts, including customers with zero orders.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER);
inserts: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Ada'); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (2, 'Ben'); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (3, 'Cara');
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (101, 1); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (102, 1); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (103, 3);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY c.customer_id;
hidden_variants: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY c.customer_id;

tasks.question: List departments with an average salary above 70,000.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (employee_id INTEGER, dept TEXT, salary REAL);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT dept, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > 70000 ORDER BY dept;
hidden_variants: SELECT dept, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > 70000 ORDER BY dept;

tasks.question: Rank employees by salary with ties sharing the same rank.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (employee_id INTEGER, name TEXT, salary REAL);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC, name;
hidden_variants: SELECT name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC, name;

tasks.question: Return rows where a customer is active and either premium or older than 30 days in the system.
tasks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INTEGER, is_active INTEGER, is_premium INTEGER, days_since_signup INTEGER);
tasks.reference_query: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE is_active = 1 AND (is_premium = 1 OR days_since_signup > 30) ORDER BY customer_id;
hidden_variants: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE is_active = 1 AND (is_premium = 1 OR days_since_signup > 30) ORDER BY customer_id;
